key_insight: A CT-based self-supervised foundation model (CIPHER) can predict which lung cancer patients are at higher risk of immune checkpoint inhibitor–induced pneumonitis before treatment starts.
clinical_relevance: If validated in broader settings, this could help clinicians identify patients needing closer monitoring or more tailored immunotherapy planning.
method: Pretrained on 590,284 CT slices from 2,500 NSCLC patients using contrastive learning plus a transformer-based masked autoencoder.
Fine-tuned on an internal immunotherapy cohort, using only non-pneumonitis cases for training and a held-out validation set for evaluation.
Benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and ensemble models, then tested in an external Johns Hopkins NSCLC cohort.
evidence_signal: CIPHER achieved AUCs of 0.77–0.85 internally, AUC 0.83 in head-to-head testing, and AUC 0.83 with 81.7% balanced accuracy in external validation.
watch_item: This is a retrospective model study, so prospective validation and site-to-site generalizability are still needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: CT-Based Deep Foundation Model for Predicting Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Induced Pneumonitis Risk in Lung Cancer
